paper_cards.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining
paper_cards.data: 518.5M frames (about 6,400 hours) of egocentric human and robot data in an 80-D unified action space.
paper_cards.method: Modular WAM infrastructure plus controlled studies of encoders, video backbones, architectures, interaction, data recipes, and synchronized joint denoising; findings instantiate OpenWAM-alpha.
paper_cards.task: Pretrain and evaluate generalist world-action models across eight simulation benchmarks and three real-robot platforms.
paper_cards.novelty: Turns coupled WAM design into a controlled modular program and releases the resulting full stack.
paper_cards.evidence: Official page reports 4 encoders, 5 backbones, 6 architectures, 8 simulation benchmarks, 3 real-robot platforms, and full code/model/data recipe release.

claim_checks.claim: Code, pretrained models, data recipes and evaluation protocols released
claim_checks.notes: Official repository and linked model organization.

paper_cards.limitations: Very new arXiv release; headline cross-benchmark comparisons are source-reported and large-scale reproduction is expensive.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct reference implementation for world/action coupling, shared action spaces, simulator evaluation, and reproducible WAM ablations.

paper_cards.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
paper_cards.data: GUMI human/GUI-agent demonstrations, released corpus, six LoRA adapters, simulation and real-robot evaluations across Franka and AgileX embodiments.
paper_cards.method: A compact semantic action vocabulary is grounded by embodiment-specific interpreters; perception/reasoning/action plugins close the VLM control loop.
paper_cards.task: Enable frontier and small open VLMs to directly control heterogeneous robots and collect demonstrations through a GUI.
paper_cards.novelty: Makes the control interface, rather than a new large action model, the reusable cross-embodiment abstraction.
paper_cards.evidence: Official page reports cross-task 89%/86%, cross-environment 100%/88%, and cross-embodiment 93%/87% for zero-shot/fine-tuned routes, with code, adapters, data and robot demos.

claim_checks.claim: Public harness, collectors, plugins, training pipeline, adapters and data

claim_checks.notes: Official project result cards; not independently reproduced.

paper_cards.limitations: Semantic action units depend on calibrated interpreters and are slower for frontier API VLMs; broad claims come from limited task/robot suites.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Reusable embodied action schema, interface contract, safety-bound interpreter, and low-cost demonstration collection pattern.

paper_cards.title: ActSafeGuard: Differentiable and Training-Aligned Constraint Enforcement for Flow-Matching Policies
paper_cards.data: Experiments on pi0.5 and Fast-WAM across constrained manipulation tasks.
paper_cards.method: Analytical ray-shooting rescales each discrete flow update to the nearest feasible-set boundary while preserving differentiability and boundary-sliding gradients.
paper_cards.task: Train and deploy flow-matching VLA/WAM action policies with hard per-step feasibility guarantees.
paper_cards.novelty: Integrates deterministic constraint enforcement into both training and inference instead of applying only an inference-time correction.
paper_cards.evidence: Paper reports 100% step safety with task success preserved or improved; the paper provides a construction-level safety proposition and four figures.

claim_checks.notes: Reported in the primary paper; not independently reproduced.
Equations 5-14 and propositions describe the mechanism.

paper_cards.limitations: Only eight pages, no public code/project page found, convex/polyhedral constraint construction is narrower than general contact safety.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Provides an executable action-validity layer and training-aligned safety primitive for flow-based VLA/WAM systems.

paper_cards.title: HaWMPO: Hallucination-Aware World Model-based Policy Optimization for Generalist Robot Policy
paper_cards.data: LIBERO Spatial/Goal/Object suites, 50 human-labeled video chunks across 10 tasks, and two real G1 tasks with 20 trials per method/task.
paper_cards.method: An action-conditioned hallucination model scores eight-frame imagined chunks using visual/context/action features; Reward-Soft downweights unreliable rollouts inside GRPO.
paper_cards.task: Post-train a generalist VLA inside a video-world-model simulator without letting hallucinated rollouts dominate learning.
paper_cards.novelty: Adds an explicit learned reliability signal to world-model policy optimization rather than treating all imagined trajectories equally.
paper_cards.evidence: Primary paper reports 63.7% LIBERO average, 80% real-robot average, HAM AUROC 0.9375 and AP 0.8952; it explicitly labels physical results preliminary.

claim_checks.claim: LIBERO average 63.7%, +2.8 points over strongest reproduced baseline
claim_checks.notes: Table 1; WoVR comparison uses a reproduced variant without original PACE.

paper_cards.limitations: No official project, code, checkpoint, or robot video was found; only two simple physical tasks; hallucination labels cover 50 chunks and the proxy is not a physical-validity guarantee.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Highly direct simulator-reliability and synthetic-rollout filtering reference, pending visual/demo verification.

paper_cards.title: Gamma-World: Generative Multi-Agent World Modeling Beyond Two Players
paper_cards.data: Synchronized multi-agent gameplay and real multi-robot sequences; training/inference pipeline and checkpoints are released.
paper_cards.method: Simplex Rotary Agent Encoding gives permutation-equivalent identities; Sparse Hub Attention reduces cross-agent communication from quadratic to linear; a distilled block-causal student streams at 24 FPS.
paper_cards.task: Generate one action-responsive, consistent world for multiple independently controlled agents.
paper_cards.novelty: Extends interactive video world models beyond one action stream while preserving independent control, shared-world consistency, and efficient streaming.
paper_cards.evidence: Official paper/project reports better fidelity, action control and inter-agent consistency than slot/dense baselines, zero-shot two-to-four-agent generalization, and 24 FPS streaming.

claim_checks.notes: Primary abstract and official gallery; not independently reproduced.

paper_cards.limitations: Interactive worlds are video rollouts rather than explicit executable geometry; quantitative evidence is concentrated in curated environments and real-robot scope is limited.
paper_cards.project_relevance: Direct multi-agent world-generation architecture and evaluation reference for synchronized embodied interactions.
